recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Any broader cleanup of narrative wording around "structured data" should be handled as a separate tracker rather than as an FHIR-18494 correction.
issue_request: FHIR-18494 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-core narrative clarification asking to replace "the structured data in the content" with "the core elements defined in the resource" in both NarrativeStatus code definitions because "structured data" could include extensions while the intended meaning was core elements.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by git commit 7550ccbfa75eb4cc50e7e55464bc52a7dce037b3, cited in the Jira comments as GH#7550ccbfa7. That commit changed the generated and extensions rows in source/datatypes/narrative.xml from the ambiguous structured-data phrase to core-elements wording.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Narrative as an active infrastructure type and maps the narrative type page, so the inspected spreadsheet source is in current build scope. Current source no longer contains the exact obsolete phrase. The additional NarrativeStatus code still uses broader "structured data" wording, but that was not one of the two targeted phrase occurrences, and later FHIR-38659 resolved no-change on changing additional-status semantics. Community searches found no direct FHIR-18494 references or conflicting minutes.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source says the generated and extensions narrative statuses are generated from core elements, preserving the approved semantic change even though the historical application used "core elements in the content" rather than the exact proposed phrase.

related_jiras.note: Later no-change request considered changing how the additional NarrativeStatus code is interpreted and left that status family unchanged.
Later narrative safety clarification added guidance around Narrative.status and core elements without contradicting the FHIR-18494 wording fix.
